limitations: A custom metal replacement flange with accessory ear is proposed; OEM approval and actual T1 adapter data are absent
The original arm/hand axial stack is not redesigned or certified by these parts
Printed PA12 is a material candidate; creep, fatigue, solvent compatibility and dynamic deflection are unverified
The low-profile carriers are geometric designs, not validated stiffness or manufacturing-process specifications
D405 is a documented camera candidate, not a confirmed camera selection; ideal60-degree source views are not its hardware calibration
Public CAD and URDF visual meshes differ; their model-based coordinate registration is not a measured hardware calibration
Connector keepouts are design allowances, not verified cable dimensions or full-motion cable routing
Source V31 replay/sweep and actual T1 fit must be reported separately from static CAD checks
Render STL files are in metres; CAD STEP and review-print STL files are in millimetres and are not released for manufacture
The actual T1-to-Sharpa adapter and its mating stack are unresolved; no replacement mating surface is synthesized.
Hand-side display assemblies are proposals, not validated installation on T1 or approval to modify hand hardware.
Camera envelopes are the supplied CAD candidates, not identification of the original T1 camera or physical D405 calibration.
Onboard optics are the unchanged supplied ideal simulated camera specifications, not measured hardware calibration.
The inherited head-only near-clipping approximation can bypass the original closed head shell; it is not physical clearance.
Static review views isolate the hand and supplied parts only; native onboard views retain all original Replay occluders.
No physical fit, assembly access, stiffness, load capacity, dynamics, or clearance pass is inferred from these images.
The source V31 grasp/stability acceptance is not changed by this visualization.
